newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bulgaria's president-elect says reforms vital.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's president-elect says reforms vital.

text.p: Bulgarian president-elect Petar Stoyanov said in an interview that an agreement between the political groups on economic reform was needed to solve his country's crisis, Spain's El Pais daily reported on Saturday.
Stoyanov, who won presidential elections in November and is due to be sworn in on Sunday, said that granting the ruling Socialists a mandate to form a new government would not resolve the crisis.
Bulgaria on Saturday witnessed a 13th day of protests led by the opposition Union of Democratic forces (UDF), which is calling for early elections.
"I have said that granting a mandate to the Socialists is not going to resolve the crisis, nor make people return to their homes," Stoyanov told El Pais.
"What is needed is an agreement between the politicial forces on at least one fundamental point: immediate economic reform," he said.
Stoyanov, had said in the past he might offer the Socialists the new mandate denied them by his predecessor Zhelyu Zhelev.
But the opposition adamantly opposes any mandate and is demanding early elections which the Socialists would almost certainly lose.
Stoyanov said the people of Bulgaria would be key to the decision on the timing of elections.
"The people in the street represent a very important political factor...Given that we need immediate economic measures, spring may be one of the most suitable options (for elections)," he said.
He said he was optimistic that the current deadlock would not paralyse the country and that an agreement could be reached between the government and the opposition.

"During the last week the ruling party and the opposition have come closer on at least two important points: the holding of future elections and their willingness to negotiate on a shock plan against the crisis," he said.
If the two sides can be drawn closer on these two points, he said, an agreement on other key issues could be reached.
"The main problem is that no government will be able to control the situation in Bulgaria if it doesn't receive the support of the current or future opposition," he added.
